items.stem: In Scala, why is Option preferred over returning null for a possibly-absent value?

options.text: It makes absence explicit in the type and forces the caller to handle it
options.rationale: Correct: Option[T] encodes Some/None so the compiler and reader see the possibility of no value.

options.text: It runs faster than returning null
options.rationale: The benefit is safety and clarity, not raw speed.

options.text: It prevents the method from ever failing
options.rationale: Option models absence; it does not stop all failures.

items.explanation: Correct: Option[T] encodes Some/None so the compiler and reader see the possibility of no value.

items.stem: Which statements about Scala are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Case classes provide pattern matching and value-based equality
options.rationale: Correct: case classes generate equals and support match extraction.

options.text: Traits can be mixed into a class to compose behaviour
options.rationale: Correct: multiple traits can be combined via mixin composition.

options.text: Scala has no support for immutable collections
options.rationale: Immutable collections are the default and are first-class.

options.text: Functions cannot be passed as arguments
options.rationale: Functions are first-class values in Scala.

items.explanation: Correct: case classes generate equals and support match extraction.; Correct: multiple traits can be combined via mixin composition.

items.stem: What does a Future[T] represent in Scala?

options.text: A value that may become available later, computed asynchronously
options.rationale: Correct: a Future holds the eventual result of an asynchronous computation.
The result is eventual, not immediate.

options.text: A mutable variable shared across threads
options.rationale: A Future is a read-once eventual result, not a shared mutable variable.
Its value is produced at run time, not at compile time.

items.explanation: Correct: a Future holds the eventual result of an asynchronous computation.
